content.text: The text reviews diseases of the liver, biliary passages, portal vein, parasites, pancreas, and peritoneum. Amyloid liver causes silent, firm enlargement associated with chronic suppuration, syphilis, malaria, cachexia, renal disease, ascites, diarrhea, and eventual exhaustion. Fatty liver reflects excess fat, alcoholism, impaired oxidation, and obesity; it produces smooth enlargement and digestive symptoms and may improve with diet and management. Bile-duct catarrh, gallstones, and obstruction cause jaundice, colic, digestive disturbance, hepatic damage, and sometimes fatal cholaemia. Portal thrombosis and suppurative pylephlebitis cause ascites, hemorrhage, fever, and hepatic abscesses. Hydatid cysts enlarge slowly and require aspiration or surgery. Pancreatic inflammation, obstruction, cancer, and degeneration cause epigastric pain, wasting, fatty stools, jaundice, and diabetes. Peritonitis produces abdominal pain, rigidity, distension, vomiting, tachycardia, and often death. John moved to the hallway; John journeyed to the kitchen.
